newsitem.title: USA: South Korea chicken imports may zoom - U.S. attache.
newsitem.headline: South Korea chicken imports may zoom - U.S. attache.

text.p: South Korea may become a booming market for chicken imports in the near future with China challenging the United States for market share, the U.S. agricultural attache in Seoul said in a report Monday.

"Some industry observers estimated imports could reach 150,000 tonnes by the year 2000," attache David Schoonover wrote, although there was a consensus of little immediate impact from the July 1997 end of import quotas.
More than 6,000 tonnes of chicken had been imported by mid- August, suggesting the 1996 quota of 10,400 tonnes would be filled. The 1995 import quota of 7,700 was not met.
U.S. chicken, mostly in the form of chicken legs, accounted for 97 percent of 1995's imports. U.S. market share has remained above 90 percent this year, Schoonover said.
When South Korea removes its tariff-rate quota in July 1997, a 30.2 percent tariff would be in place.
The higher tariff and the need to establish trading relationships were expected to constrain imports in 1997.
South Korea was forecast to consume 480,000 tonnes of poultry meat in 1997, compared to 465,000 this year.
"Beyond 1997...changes are expected to occur relatively rapidly, Schoonover said.

"The large (domestic) integrators are expected to become the major importers and distribute the imported chicken through their own distribution channels. China is expected to enter the market in a major way and eventually reach the market share it currently enjoys in Japan," the attache wrote.
South Korean officials say the domestic industry would become more competitive in coming years and the government projects imports of 50,000 tonnes in 2004, or 13 percent of the market.
Industry officials say imports could reach 20-30 percent in the next few years, Schoonover said.
